overclaims: The study found toxic output even from innocuous prompts.
checks.note: The statement excerpt, proposition, axis, horizon and supported outcome are all correct, and the Microsoft clause is properly left ungraded. Two problems: (1) e1's published excerpt is cut to 'seemingly innocuous prompts.', which drops the actual finding that pretrained LMs can degenerate into toxic text, so the citation no longer shows what it supports. (2) The rationale says 'innocuous prompts' without the source's qualifier 'seemingly', which overstates the finding.

The excerpt, proposition, conditions, unresolved outcome and rationale are all consistent with the frozen case and its evidence. The citation excerpts are cut so far that they misstate the sources. e3 is the single word 'disclose', which loses that s.17940 requires bots to disclose they are bots. e1 'is voluntary' loses its subject, the AI RMF and Playbook. e2 drops 'for the development or use of AI or prohibitions on AI use', and in context 'None' refers to the other AI-related laws on training and sector-specific use.
